environment: Ryzen 9 6900HS, Ubuntu/WSL, CPU, debug build, two ONNX threads; local observations, not production sizing
limitations: 64 authored supported and four unsupported questions over 58 seed artifacts, not independent collector queries. No training or fine-tuning. Unsupported questions still return nearest candidates. Rerank timings include candidate-source reads and publication/hash rechecks but exclude initial query embedding/retrieval. Other development work ran during portions of these measurements.

queries.question: Where can I buy second-hand clothes and furniture rather than throw useful things away?
Which building uses large panels of glued wood instead of much of its steel and concrete?
Where is sunlight used to preheat water before the heating plant makes steam?
Which place combines farming with panels that generate electricity?
Where is collected rainwater stored underground and reused by the Life Science Laboratories?
How are used pipette tip boxes turned back into new laboratory plastics?
Where do plants and soil help absorb rain runoff rather than send it straight into storm drains?
Where can I step into a rainforest room and warm up on my way to class in winter?
My phone battery is dying while I wait for the bus. Is there a place powered by the sun where I can plug it in?
How can students travel into neighboring towns without paying for a bus ticket?
Where can I charge an electric car in the Campus Center Parking Garage?
Can I borrow an electric bicycle at one station and leave it at a different station?
Our university department has spare desks. Where can another department get them instead of buying new furniture?
Which garden provides food and water for bees, butterflies and hummingbirds?
Which garden grows fresh produce for the Amherst Survival Center and a community meal program?
Which garden replaced a lawn beside Franklin Dining Commons and supplies it with fruit, vegetables and herbs?
Where were food plants from India grown at the chancellor's residence?
What installation warms returning water with sunlight so the steam plant needs to burn less gas?
Where is treated sewage cleaned further and used in boilers instead of drinking water?
Which campus facility produces both electricity and the steam used to heat and cool buildings?
Which economics building was designed to make as much energy as it consumes each year?
Where is the first solar parking canopy in the UMass system, beside the visitor center?
Which computing laboratory building completed in 2025 was the first on campus to earn LEED Platinum?
Which basketball practice building earned LEED Gold and has rooftop solar?
Which campus gym generates electricity from panels on its large flat roof?
Which physics and chemistry research building was designed so its laboratories can be rearranged instead of demolishing the building?
Where is a public courtyard with native plants and built-in seating on the Design Building roof?
Which underground tank can store up to 10,000 gallons of rainwater for laboratory and landscape uses?
What green-building rating system awards Certified, Silver, Gold or Platinum based on earned points?
How is most of the campus landscape maintained without artificial pesticides or fertilizers?
Which ILC roof has about 15,000 square feet of hardy sedum plants instead of bare roofing?
Where is Durfee conservatry?
Where is the campus nuclear fusion reactor?
Which campus office renews foreign passports?
Where is the campus aquarium containing deep-sea sharks?
Which campus rocket launch pad sends satellites into orbit?
I need a little tropical escape between lectures when everything outdoors is freezing. What place fits?
Our lab keeps throwing away the rigid boxes left after pipetting. Is there a way to give that plastic another life?
I'm furnishing my student room on a tiny budget and need a used jacket too. Where should I look?
Our academic unit needs cabinets another unit no longer wants. Is there a university reuse showroom?
Where can animals graze underneath equipment that harvests sunshine?
How does the university avoid boiling perfectly drinkable water when it could use cleaned wastewater?
What uses free warmth from the sky to reduce the fuel needed to turn returning water into steam?
Is there a growing space whose harvest helps neighbors struggling to get enough to eat?
I want to see a planted habitat that gives nectar-seeking insects and hummingbirds food and water. Where should I look?
How does the university look after its grounds while avoiding manufactured weed and bug treatments?
Which home of the people who study markets balances the power it consumes with power it makes?
Where can students work out beneath a rooftop that harvests sunlight for electricity?
Can I sit among native plants above the architecture school's building rather than at ground level?
Which research facility can keep changing its laboratory layout as experiments change, rather than being knocked down?
What planted hollow beside the architecture building catches water from the roof so it can seep away?
What certification tells me how well a structure scored on saving resources, with a precious-metal top tier?

I'm new here and don't know the names of places. My laptop is almost dead, I'm waiting for public transport, and I would like an outdoor plug that gets its power from sunshine. What artifact should I look at?
I don't have a car and I am trying to spend less this semester. I remember hearing students could buy things other students left behind at move-out, like clothes and lamps. Which place is that?
This probably sounds vague, but a friend mentioned a quiet place on campus with tropical plants where people warm up during winter between classes. I forgot its name. Can you find it?

I'm not asking about the pond or the power station. I mean the tank hidden below the Life Science Laboratories landscape that saves rain for things that don't require drinking-quality water. What is it?

There are so many sustainability projects that I can't remember which is which. The one I mean collects empty pipette boxes and sends the material back into making laboratory supplies, instead of treating it all as garbage.

Someone told me there is an architecture and construction teaching building made from layers of wood glued into big structural panels. I am interested in the material, not gardens or solar panels. Which building?
I saw a project where raising electricity-generating panels higher left room underneath for crops or livestock. It was university agricultural land rather than a parking lot. Which project was that?
I'd rather not drive or rent a bicycle. I am a student trying to reach the neighboring towns using frequent public transport without buying a ticket. Which campus service should I read about?

I mean the training home of the basketball teams with solar on its roof, not the general student gym. Which building is it?
